writeup_source_quote: The stance-contrast idea (think/don't-think) is known from White-Bear Steering (ref-05), which used the bench's own `directed_modulation` items. My contribution is a new, self-authored, lexically varied contrast set (six distinct stance-verb families, my own concepts and carriers), and a re-tuned dose for this metric's three read layers (26, 28, 30): the optimum moves to a much larger total push (scale 1.9) than the five-read-layer setting.
rationale: Both the write-up and the closing message identify White-Bear Steering (ref-05) as the origin of the stance-contrast idea and both describe it as having used the bench's own directed_modulation items. Both claim the same novelty — a self-authored, lexically varied contrast set plus a re-tuned dose for the three read layers (26, 28, 30) with a much larger optimal push — and all reported numbers (pass@10 0.1275→0.7745, mean log10 rank 2.33→0.73, random-vector control at 0.1275, reversed-direction control at 0.049) match exactly, with no claims in the message about the write-up document itself to check.
